newsitem.title: CHINA: China to export more electronics in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China to export more electronics in 1997 - paper.

text.p: China's Ministry of Electronics Industry expects electronics exports will hit $24 billion in 1997, up about 15 percent from 1996, the China Daily said.
More than half of the output will be sold abroad, the ministry was quoted on Friday as saying.

In 1997, China expects to export five million colour television sets, 4.36 million colour television tubes, 1.25 million lines of computerised digital telephone exchanges, 650,000 micro-computers and 1.18 million video cassette recorders, the Ministry said.

Foreign-funded enterprises have become a major force in production for export, it said. At present, 42 percent of colour television set makers and 40 percent of computerised digital telephones switch plants were funded from overseas, it said.
In the first 11 months of 1996, electronics exports were $18.97 billion, up 29.8 percent from the same 1995 period. Imports totalled $15.66 billion, up 18 percent, it said.

The three major import items were telecommunications, computers and related parts and components, integrated circuits and relevant micro-electronics, which were valued at a combined $9.92 billion, or 63.6 percent of total imports last year, the Ministry said. -- Beijing newsroom (8610) 6532-1921
